findings.title: Sector goldens cannot change only in version fields
findings.claim: The required version bump necessarily changes stored sector hashes, so the stated re-bless diff is impossible.
findings.evidence: spec L76-L77, L94; src/renderer/src/sim/flatten.ts:L45-L50; src/shared/hash.ts:L3-L10; tests/golden.test.ts:L27-L31
findings.why: The golden test compares hashes computed from a flattened state containing SIM_VERSION. Changing 35 to 36 changes those hashes even when gameplay is identical.
findings.fix: Require version fields and their derived hashes to be re-blessed. Prove the version-only gameplay change by comparing all other canonical values and gameplay traces.

findings.title: The runtime fallback drops the binding ten-seed gate
findings.claim: The proposed default three-seed smoke run would leave seeds 4 to 10 unchecked in the full suite.
findings.why: The parent makes the seeds 1 to 10 result an H-0 gate.
findings.fix: Keep all ten seeds in the required gate run. If needed, add a separate three-seed smoke test without substituting it for the gate.

findings.title: The scripted flight and firing policy needs exact rules
findings.claim: The Helm’s orbit, alignment and avoidance choices and the gunner’s missile cadence and release rule leave multiple materially different implementations.
findings.why: The plan writer cannot derive one deterministic policy or expected gate results from phrases such as “brings the nose round” and “every so often.”
findings.fix: Specify the state transitions, numerical thresholds, turn and thrust choices, line-of-sight rule, missile interval, priority order and tie breaks, with the pair’s tunable constants named.

findings.title: Repair assignment contradicts the nearest-character rule
findings.claim: The spec assigns Engines to the Helm while also requiring the nearest character to take a repair.
findings.why: The parent’s walk distances put the gunner about 6 tiles from Engines and the Helm about 27 tiles away. The two rules select different repairers.
findings.fix: Choose one assignment rule and specify priority and tie breaks when several rooms are damaged.

findings.title: A planet-contact ending has no defined attribution
findings.claim: The gate asks whether a duel ended from planet contact, but the proposed telemetry observes contact counters while the outcome is decided after all damage in the tick.
findings.why: A planet hit and another lethal hit can occur in one tick. A counter change and final outcome do not identify which damage caused the ending.
findings.fix: Define terminal-cause precedence and record the necessary per-damage event, or state an explicit observable proxy for this gate.

findings.title: The bait proxy contradicts its telemetry definition
findings.claim: The proposed count requires proximity and turning at contact, while the stated bait measure requires a preceding manoeuvre within five seconds that brought the hunter toward the obstacle.
findings.why: The proxy can count unrelated contacts and miss contacts after the crew stops turning.
findings.fix: Define a tick-stamped manoeuvre condition, its direction test and the 300-tick window; then count qualifying enemy contacts against that definition.

findings.title: Weapons can have work while its missile is in flight
findings.claim: The proposed “nothing to do” condition counts missile flight as idle even though the gunner steers that missile.
findings.why: This overstates idle time during one of the gunner’s required activities.
findings.fix: Exclude ticks with an attended missile in flight, and specify the remaining idle predicate precisely.

findings.title: The duel hash does not include SIM_VERSION
findings.claim: The spec says SIM_VERSION is hashed into every flattened state, but neither tactical nor duel flattening includes it.
findings.why: The new duel golden would not distinguish a version change unless its fixture checks the version separately.
findings.fix: Include SIM_VERSION in flattenDuel, or require and verify an explicit version field in the duel golden.

findings.title: Per-player repair start and finish events need semantics
findings.claim: The proposed events do not define a start after interrupted work or who receives finish credit when two players repair together.
findings.why: The existing repair phase reduces each player to a per-room holder count, so those per-player transitions cannot be inferred from its current data alone.
findings.fix: Define start and finish attribution, including resumed and joint work, and specify whether previous holder state lives in the duel state or is derived by the telemetry accumulator.

findings.title: Missile-to-missile losses are omitted
findings.claim: The telemetry cause list omits the existing `missile` ending cause.
findings.why: Those losses would have no specified bucket in the per-ship totals.
findings.fix: Add missile-to-missile collision to the loss causes.
